authority: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Ministry of Finance

description.en: Registration under the Goods and Services Tax regime for businesses and individuals engaged in the supply of goods or services, administered through the GST Common Portal.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Businesses engaged in supply of goods (general category states)
verifiedConditions.claim: GST registration is mandatory for businesses with aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 40 lakhs for supply of goods in general category states.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Businesses engaged in supply of services
verifiedConditions.claim: GST registration is mandatory for businesses with aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 20 lakhs for supply of services.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Any person making interstate taxable supply
verifiedConditions.claim: GST registration is mandatory for any person making interstate taxable supply of goods or services, irrespective of turnover.
E-commerce operators are required to obtain GST registration irrespective of turnover.

unverifiedEligibility: Special category states have a lower threshold of Rs. 20 lakhs for goods and Rs. 10 lakhs for services.
Casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons must also register irrespective of turnover.
Persons required to pay tax under reverse charge mechanism must register.
This record does not cover voluntary registration or input service distributor registration.

requirements.claim: PAN (Permanent Account Number) of the business or proprietor is mandatory for GST registration.
Aadhaar number of the primary authorized signatory is required for GST registration and Aadhaar authentication.
Proof of principal place of business is required, such as electricity bill, rent agreement, property tax receipt, or ownership deed.
Bank account details (cancelled cheque or bank statement) are required. Bank details can be furnished within 45 days of grant of registration.
Photographs of the proprietor/partners/directors/authorized signatory are required.
Document of constitution of business is required: Partnership Deed for partnership firms, Certificate of Incorporation for companies, or Registration Certificate for other entities.
Letter of authorization or board resolution for the authorized signatory, applicable for companies and LLPs.

processInformation.claim: Navigate to the GST Common Portal (gst.gov.in) and select 'Services > Registration > New Registration' under the Taxpayers tab.
Fill Part A of Form GST REG-01 with PAN, mobile number, and email address. OTP verification is performed on both mobile and email.
A Temporary Reference Number (TRN) is generated after successful OTP verification of Part A.

Using the TRN, fill Part B of Form GST REG-01 with business details, promoter/partner information, authorized signatory details, place of business, goods/services details, bank account information, and upload required documents.
Aadhaar authentication of the primary authorized signatory is performed. If Aadhaar authentication is opted out, the application is processed with physical verification of the place of business.
Upon submission, an Application Reference Number (ARN) is generated and sent to the applicant via email and SMS. The application is forwarded to the jurisdictional GST officer for processing.

The jurisdictional officer may approve, reject, or seek clarification on the application within the prescribed processing time. If clarification is sought, the applicant must respond within 7 working days.
Upon approval, GSTIN (Goods and Services Tax Identification Number) and Registration Certificate in Form GST REG-06 are issued electronically.

output.claim: A GST Registration Certificate in Form GST REG-06 is issued containing the 15-digit GSTIN, effective date of registration, and details of the registered person. The certificate is available for download from the GST portal.

fees.applicability: New GST registration through the GST Common Portal
fees.claim: GST registration is free of cost. No government fee is charged for new GST registration.
No authorized service-centre charge is established by the reviewed sources. Third-party consultants or CA firms may charge separately.

processingTime.applicability: New GST registration with Aadhaar authentication completed
processingTime.claim: GST registration is typically processed within 3 working days if Aadhaar authentication is completed. Without Aadhaar authentication, physical verification may extend the timeline up to 7 working days.

sources.title: GST Common Portal — Registration
sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN), Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The GST portal provides the official registration facility including Form GST REG-01, eligibility criteria, document requirements, Aadhaar authentication, and processing timelines.
claimsSupported: GST registration is mandatory for businesses exceeding the prescribed turnover thresholds.
The turnover threshold is Rs. 40 lakhs for goods and Rs. 20 lakhs for services in general category states.
Registration is done online through the GST Common Portal using Form GST REG-01.
PAN, Aadhaar, business address proof, bank details, photographs, and constitution documents are required.
GSTIN and Registration Certificate in Form GST REG-06 are issued upon approval.
sources.uncertainty: Processing timelines may vary based on jurisdictional officer workload and completeness of application.

sources.title: CBIC GST Portal
sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The CBIC portal provides official GST rules, notifications, and circulars governing the registration process.
claimsSupported: CBIC is the administrative authority for GST.
GST registration rules and procedures are governed by CBIC notifications.
sources.uncertainty: The CBIC portal is a policy reference; actual registration is performed on gst.gov.in.

sources.title: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Section 22 prescribes mandatory registration for persons whose aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold. Section 24 lists persons who must register irrespective of turnover including interstate suppliers and e-commerce operators. Section 25 governs the registration procedure.
claimsSupported: Registration is mandatory for persons with turnover exceeding the prescribed threshold under Section 22.
Interstate suppliers and e-commerce operators must register irrespective of turnover under Section 24.
Registration procedure and timelines are prescribed under Sections 25-26.
Constitution documents are required as part of the registration application.
sources.uncertainty: The Act has been amended multiple times; threshold limits in special category states differ from general category states.

limitations: This record covers new GST registration for regular taxpayers only. It does not cover composition scheme registration, ISD registration, TDS/TCS registration, or non-resident taxable person registration.
Turnover thresholds for special category states (Rs. 20 lakhs for goods, Rs. 10 lakhs for services) are noted but not fully modeled.
The record does not cover GST registration amendment, cancellation, suspension, or revocation processes.
Third-party professional service charges for GST registration assistance are not established.
State-specific variations in physical verification procedures are not covered.

review.reviewReason: Core registration evidence is reviewed, but composition scheme, special category states, and additional registration types remain unmodeled.
nextReviewTrigger: Changes to GST turnover thresholds by GST Council notification.
Amendments to Section 22 or Section 24 of the CGST Act.
Changes to the GST registration form or portal process.
Introduction of new registration categories or document requirements.
